newsitem.title: USA: Ultradata finding new sales outlets.
newsitem.headline: Ultradata finding new sales outlets.

text.p: Ultradata Systems Inc, which posted lower fourth-quarter and yearend earnings, said it was establishing new distribution channels for its handheld travel computer products, including Sears Roebuck & Co department stores.

It said Road Whiz products now are being sold by major electronics retailers, office superstores and specialty catalogers. A custom travel product, Sears Pathfinder, will be sold in more than 800 stores beginning in April.

Ultradata cited substantially lower sales in 1996 to the QVC Network as the reason for its weaker performance. It said QVC sales for fiscal 1996 totaled $616,000 compared to $4.5 million in fiscal 1995.
The company also said it anticipates releasing new products during the first half of 1997.

Ultradata reported fourth-quarter earnings per diluted share of $0.20, down from $0.26. Sales were $5.0 million, up from $4.7 million. For the year, earnings declined to $0.08 from $0.49 per diluted share, and sales fell to $9.1 million from $10.1 million.
